context.hint: The policy-local decoder removed semicolon-terminated numeric and named entity variants of a disallowed scheme from link attributes while keeping allowed and relative link values byte-identical; the full local suite passed. The next uncertainty is breadth: the URI branch is shared by image source, video poster, form action, cite/background and SVG link attributes, and malformed or nested references may expose crashes or missed forms. The attacker still controls only the markup and uses a disposable local Python fixture. The next step is a robustness matrix over every URI attribute class and degenerate reference form.
context.surface: Python library made of a streaming HTML tokenizer, an attribute policy filter and an entity-preserving serializer. Untrusted markup enters through a sanitize API configured with allowed tags, allowed attributes and allowed URI schemes.
assumptions: The attacker controls the entire untrusted HTML fragment but not the sanitizer configuration or the local filesystem.
Allowed attributes include at least one URI-valued attribute on a link, an image, a video poster, a form action, a cite/background attribute and an SVG link.
The sanitizer's protocol list is configurable; http, https and mailto are allowed by default and a caller may add a custom scheme.
All experiments use a disposable local Python environment and in-memory strings; no network service or public target is involved.
The official benchmark evaluator is external; local test results are not an official pass.

incumbent.text: Hypothesis: decoding every named and numeric HTML character reference for the URI policy comparison will remove entity-hidden disallowed schemes, because the serializer keeps the original reference spelling while the policy sees the resolved scheme. Prerequisite: a policy-local decoder built from the parser's named-entity table plus decimal and hexadecimal numeric parsing. Bounded test: sanitize link attributes containing hex, decimal, uppercase-hex, named-colon, named-tab, named-newline and numeric-control variants of javascript: and file:, then compare against allowed http(s), mailto, relative, query-ampersand and custom-protocol controls. Expected result: all entity-hidden disallowed values lose the URI attribute; allowed and relative values keep their exact serialized bytes. Falsifier: any entity-hidden scheme survives, or any allowed control changes bytes. Cleanup: revert the one policy line and helper in the disposable copy; limitations: the comparison value is decoded but the emitted value intentionally stays encoded.

candidates.text: Hypothesis: the repair sits in the shared URI-attribute policy branch, so entity-hidden schemes are removed for image source, video poster, form action, cite/background and SVG link attributes exactly as for a link. Prerequisite: configure each tag and URI attribute explicitly, then use the same decoder. Bounded test: sanitize a hexadecimal javascript value on each attribute class and allowed/relative controls on the same classes; record whether any URI attribute remains and whether every control is byte-identical to the pristine output. Expected result: all malicious attributes are dropped and all controls match. Falsifier: any class retains the hidden scheme or differs on an allowed value. Cleanup: use a disposable fixture. Limitations: SVG namespace handling may differ from plain attributes.

Hypothesis: malformed, empty, surrogate or out-of-range numeric references can raise during character conversion or silently corrupt the policy value. Prerequisite: a decoder that catches conversion errors. Bounded test: sanitize link values containing an empty numeric reference, an overflowing hexadecimal value, an overflowing decimal value, a surrogate code point and an unknown named reference; compare output bytes before and after the patch and verify no exception escapes. Expected result: no exception, controls unchanged, and no malformed value becomes a blocked scheme. Falsifier: any exception or control drift. Cleanup: remove the temporary cases. Limitations: replacement-character policy may legitimately over-reject a malformed relative value.

Hypothesis: nested or double-encoded references do not survive because the serializer resolves only one entity layer and a browser also resolves only one layer. Prerequisite: the same serializer behavior. Bounded test: sanitize a double-encoded reference and re-parse the emitted attribute once with the same HTML parser; also inspect the raw emitted bytes. Expected result: the re-parsed value is not a blocked scheme. Falsifier: any emitted attribute whose first parse yields javascript: or another blocked scheme. Cleanup: none beyond the fixture. Limitations: repeated decoding by an intermediary could change the result.

Hypothesis: non-ASCII or high-Unicode references are classified correctly because only the resolved scheme prefix is examined. Prerequisite: a decoder that returns Unicode characters. Bounded test: sanitize an allowed scheme whose first letter is a numeric reference, a relative path beginning with a named non-ASCII entity, and a high code point before a colon; compare bytes with the pristine output. Expected result: no crash and no blocked scheme. Falsifier: a non-ASCII prefix is mistaken for an allowed scheme or an allowed value changes. Cleanup: remove the fixture. Limitations: URI scheme names are ASCII, so this is mostly a robustness control.

Hypothesis: a minimal exported patch that contains only the source delta will apply to a fresh snapshot and reproduce the same behavior, whereas test files or run state in the delta will break the official handoff. Prerequisite: a pristine copy and a JSONL export containing only the source change. Bounded test: apply the patch to a fresh copy, import it, run the focused and full suites, and compare the robustness matrix with the working copy. Expected result: clean application and identical output. Falsifier: apply failure, test drift or any extra file in the patch. Cleanup: discard the fresh copy. Limitations: official evaluation remains external.

observation.summary: Ran a 22-case matrix against the patched copy and the pristine snapshot. Entity-hidden schemes were removed from link, image source, video poster, form action, blockquote cite, generic background and SVG link attributes. All allowed, relative, query-ampersand, custom-protocol, entity-encoded-http, non-ASCII-prefix, unknown-entity and double-encoded controls were byte-identical before and after, and no case raised an exception. The comparison found one remaining policy gap: a decimal numeric reference without a trailing semicolon was not decoded by the helper. The serializer escaped its ampersand, so re-parsing the pristine output yielded a relative-looking value rather than a script scheme, but the policy still failed to see the resolved prefix. Evidence strength: direct multi-attribute matrix with byte controls. Limitation: the no-semicolon form needed a separate parser-semantics check.
observation.next_hint: Decide whether the policy decoder should consume numeric digit runs without a trailing semicolon, matching HTML tokenizer termination, and keep invalid numeric references unchanged so malformed controls do not drift.
